title: A retreat, my dear boys, signifies a withdrawal for awhile from the cares of our life, the cares of this workaday world, in order to examine the state of our conscience, to reflect on the mysteries of holy religion and to understand better why we are here in this world.
html_source:
Notice how the Rector sees the world as a “workaday world,” which seems to imply a relatively mechanical nature.

The Rector contends that a “withdrawal” from “cares” and the “workaday world” affords a better place “in order to examine the state of our conscience"—a better place to think things over. Maybe he feels that getting a sort of outside view of things is a better way to reevaluate—"to reflect” on religion, purpose, etc.

(An escape from this sounds good!)
